problem: 3DGS-based instance image-goal navigation methods (GaussNav, BEINGS) randomly sample many viewpoints or trajectories to cover discriminative cues, creating redundant overlapping renders and heavy rendering and comparison cost. They lack principled view selection.
motivation: Users may give goal photos from arbitrary viewpoints, so the agent needs a continuous 3D representation that keeps texture detail. Exhaustive sampling makes this impractical. The paper instead scores the 3DGS field directly to localize the target with few forward passes.
key_idea: Build a CLIP-feature 3D Gaussian field and localize the goal instance hierarchically: global CLIP semantic scoring picks candidate regions, then local ray-to-DINOv2 cross-attention scoring and triangulation give the 6D target pose.
insight: Both scoring stages are needed. Removing global semantic scoring drops SR from 0.784 to 0.608, and removing local geometric scoring drops it to 0.421, so semantics prune the search space while geometry supplies instance-level discrimination. Scene-specific finetuning adds about 6 SR points (0.721 to 0.784). Oracle ablations show localization is the bottleneck: GT global localization reaches 0.944 SR, and GT matching reaches 0.842.
method: Gaussian reconstruction: frontier-based exploration collects RGB-D and poses, then hierarchical submap 3DGS (Gaussian-SLAM/MAGiC-SLAM style) is built with color, depth L1 and scale regularization losses.
Feature lifting: LUDVIG-style CLIP features from all frames are aggregated onto each Gaussian by a rendering-weight-weighted average.

Global semantic scoring: Mask-RCNN gives the goal object's class label, whose CLIP text embedding is compared by cosine similarity with each Gaussian feature. Thresholding then LUDVIG-style diffusion yields connected candidate regions.

Local region scoring: random Gaussians in each region emit rays (origin, direction, SH color) over the normal hemisphere. An MLP with positional encoding embeds them and cross-attends to DINOv2 goal-image features (6DGS-style). Attention summed over goal tokens gives a region score, and the top region is selected.

Fine pose estimation: denser Gaussian-ray sampling in the chosen region, top-k pairs, then triangulation gives the 6D target pose. The ray-image network is pretrained on HM3D train and finetuned per scene with the collected observations.
Path planning: Gaussians are projected to a 2D BEV map, and Fast Marching Method planning goes to the target.

setting.backbone: 3DGS field + CLIP features + Mask-RCNN detector + DINOv2 ray-image cross-attention network (pretrained on HM3D train, finetuned per scene)
setting.training_data: Local geometric scoring network trained on HM3D train scenes (145 scenes) and finetuned per test scene on its collected observations; CLIP, DINOv2 and Mask-RCNN are pretrained
setting.action_space: continuous 4-D (linear velocity, angular velocity, camera pitch velocity, stop) in Habitat; FMM planning on BEV map
setting.privileged: none stated at test time (agent explores the scene first to build the 3DGS map; GT variants appear only in ablation)

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,000 validation episodes from Krantz et al.
numbers.backbone: 3DGS + CLIP + DINOv2 ray-image cross-attention (finetuned per scene)
numbers.extra: pre-exploration to build the 3DGS map; per-scene finetuning

numbers.backbone: 3DGS + CLIP + DINOv2 ray-image cross-attention (no per-scene finetuning)

numbers_note: Split named 'validation' (1,000 episodes), recorded as val. Oracle ablation variants (GT Match, GT Global Localization) omitted as they use GT information.
results: GauScoreMap reaches 0.784 SR and 0.605 SPL on HM3D IIN validation, beating GaussNav (0.725 / 0.578) and IEVE InternImage with scene map (0.705 / 0.347). It also runs in real-world indoor tests on a humanoid agent (shown only in a video).
limitations: Static environments only; dynamic scenes with moving objects or changed layouts are not handled.
Requires pre-exploration to build the 3DGS and feature field, plus per-scene finetuning.
Relies on a detector's class label, so detection errors propagate; no efficiency or timing numbers are given despite the efficiency claims.
